title: S3 session reuse
review_status: Measured before commit · committed as a765570
summary: Reuse the aiobotocore session; still create and close an S3 client per request. Cold POST 500 first-request CPU: 0.725 → 0.577 s. Original Memray peak: 171.241 → 151.393 MiB. These do not isolate get_session() cost or prove full-process RAM savings.

cpu.procedure: 3 fresh Python processes per workload · 1 request each · 0 warm-ups. Phase values are medians; function tables show session 1.
cpu.scope: Yappi starts before application/dependency imports and stops after the first complete API response. Includes imports, startup/client setup and that response. Excludes worker/Python/Yappi bootstrap, prepared payloads, GET seeding, verification and shutdown. PostgreSQL and MinIO remain running with their caches.
cpu.reading_guide: Phase CPU: median of 3 processes. Function CPU: session 1. Self = function only; inclusive = function plus callees. The S3 client dependency row covers a new client, not just get_session().
cpu.limitation: Profiler overhead is included. These CPU seconds are not unprofiled request latency. Phase medians are independent and need not sum exactly. This is a cold application process, not a cold machine.

memory.profiler: Memray 1.17.2 via the original pytest-memray workflow
memory.scope: Peak tracked allocation for the entire benchmark test function: includes test-data generation, repeated benchmark execution and GET seeding. Client-fixture creation, application startup and earlier imports are outside capture.
memory.reading_guide: Each peak is the sum of Memray high-watermark allocation records divided by 1,048,576. S3 SDK / data is a diagnostic group whose recorded stack includes botocore or aiobotocore; the remainder is intentionally left unclassified.
memory.limitation: Not server-only RAM, RSS, per-request memory or leak evidence. The shared session can be created before Memray starts, so a lower tracked peak does not establish the same reduction in full-process memory.

findings.title: S3 client dependency
findings.interpretation: The request reuses the session created at startup; a new client is still built and closed. This row does not isolate get_session() cost.
findings.validation: Compare the same dependency function across cold profiles; time session and client construction separately before claiming a specific cause.

findings.title: Cold first request
findings.interpretation: GET 10 KB also changed from 0.346 to 0.219 CPU s. Profiler CPU is separate from benchmark latency.
findings.validation: Median of 3 fresh processes for each workload and stage.

findings.title: Whole-test memory
findings.interpretation: Lower tracked peak in the original Memray scope; shared startup allocations may now fall outside the capture.
findings.validation: Compare original Memray runs, not full-process RAM.

findings.title: POST handler remains
findings.evidence: POST handler: 0.132 inclusive CPU s · session 1
findings.interpretation: This includes several kinds of work; it does not establish database inserts as the bottleneck.
findings.validation: Measure encoding, S3 upload and database insert phases separately before choosing the next change.

limitations: The captures were made on a dirty worktree before a765570. All 12 accepted cold CPU result files identify the same application SHA-256; the final commit includes the candidate code.
The benchmark tab has one original benchmark report per stage. Its latency differences are provisional, not confidence intervals.
get_s3_client inclusive CPU covers session lookup, fresh client creation and cleanup. get_session runs once at startup in this stage; it is not a per-request client cache.
The original Memray scope omits startup and imports. Allocations moved before capture may appear as a lower peak without reducing full-process RAM.
S3 request and new TCP connection counts did not change; the separate diagnostic pass recorded POST 1/1 and GET 3/3 per request before and after.

metric_sources.rule: For each workload and phase, median of 3 accepted cold captures in summary.csv. Each capture has one request and zero warm-ups.
Session-1 cpu.pstat: selected function call count, self CPU and inclusive CPU, rounded to 6 decimals. Absent bytes.find is shown as zero. cpu.txt provides a readable view.
Original make memprofile binaries: sum high-watermark record sizes / 2^20. S3 group includes records with botocore or aiobotocore in the Python stack; the remainder is unclassified.
